threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You start asking for directions to the nearest tube, but forget that the nearest one is a bus ride away. It's all about the Overground here.
Last night on the N137, a bloke was serenading the whole bus with 90s R&B. Never heard so many folks humming along, even the driver cracked a smile.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift café in the park, complete with flower decorations and a hand-painted sign. Pure Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the U-Bahn stations are basically mini art galleries? It’s like a treasure hunt every time you ride. Keeps the commute interesting!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell a local by how they navigate a BART meltdown—while others panic, we just pull out our phones and grab a taco.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling while waiting for the 19 over by Turk. He lost his balance, dropped a ball, and a pigeon snagged it. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real gems are the quiet squares like Plaza del Sol, where locals sip vermut and swap stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand in front of Gaudí's buildings with their phones out, taking selfies for every angle, while locals just pass by with a smile.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still using Google Maps to find your way around the back streets? Locals can navigate by the scent of street food.
Caught a guy on the 35 last night trying to sell a stolen bike on the quiet. The bus driver just rolled his eyes and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me on a Sunday morning, the smell of fresh baked bread from the bakery and the sound of kids playing in the yard. That's when Neukölln felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find open-air cinemas setting up in hidden courtyards, complete with homemade popcorn stalls and locals chatting over beers.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're from the Mission when you can name at least three taco trucks, but still can’t tell you how to get to the ballpark without GPS.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 14 Mission haggling with the driver over change while blasting old school hip hop. Every Muni ride is a mini-show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plaza is just for selfies, but locals know it's where the real conversations happen at dusk.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to try the little local bakeries; they still think chocolate croissants are the best breakfast.
